ground_truth.description: The instructions hard-code resolve_ticket(timeout_seconds=60), below the server default of 115 s. On a slow curator, the client-side call can time out and return `failed` even though the curator ultimately creates the task; the agent would then report it as skipped/failed (inaccurate accounting, possible duplicate re-file) despite the task actually being created server-side.

The two-step flow only enumerates resolve_ticket statuses created/combined/failed; there is no guidance for a resolve_ticket call that returns an unexpected/missing status or that itself errors after a successful submit_task, leaving that path undefined for the agent.

task.title: Migrate orchestrator add_task callers to submit_task + resolve_ticket
task.description:
Migrate orchestrator code-path callers of the deprecated add_task MCP tool to the new submit_task + resolve_ticket flow introduced in task 919.

Scope (orchestrator subtree only):
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/review_checkpoint.py — reviewer triage creates follow-up tasks from review findings.
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py — multiple role definitions list `mcp__fused-memory__add_task` in their allowed tool set; replace with `submit_task` + `resolve_ticket` (both allowed). The steward and reviewer triage paths both call add_task via MCP.

For each callsite:
- Replace add_task(...) -> submit_task(...) + resolve_ticket(ticket, timeout_seconds=60) pattern.
- Handle status="dropped" / "combined" explicitly where behaviour depends on knowing the task id.
- Update any allowlists in role definitions.

Out of scope: reconciliation stage2 prompts (tracked separately), skill prompts (tracked separately), facade removal (tracked separately).

Depends on: 919.
